assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology led to incretin therapies that have transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefits; a rare unbroken line from basic peptide physiology to a global therapeutic class.
assessment.attribution: Holst (incretin physiology and GLP-1 secretion/action in humans), Drucker (GLP-1 biology, GLP-2, therapeutic translation) and Mojsov (peptide identification and synthesis of the active form) form a coherent three-person core. Knudsen is a credible drug-development contributor, and credit among early GLP-1 groups is contested; I cannot verify the priority claims independently.
assessment.maturity: Extensive independent confirmation through large randomized outcome trials and widespread clinical use; timing is highly appropriate.
uncertainties: Priority dispute over who first identified the active GLP-1 form and its insulinotropic action.
Whether the prize should reward basic physiology, the engineered long-acting drugs, or both.
Long-term safety and durability data are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational targeted inhibition of BCR-ABL turned chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a manageable one and established the paradigm of kinase-inhibitor therapy.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound discovery), Druker (preclinical and clinical proof of concept) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) are a natural trio. Credit for the underlying BCR-ABL oncogene work lies with others outside this entry.
assessment.maturity: Decades of follow-up with durable survival; the paradigm is fully confirmed and recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Prior recognition of oncogene and kinase foundations may lead some to see this as an application of earlier work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered CAR-T cells produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new class of living therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical translation of CD19 CAR-T with costimulatory domains) and Sadelain (CAR design and costimulation concepts) are the strongest pair; Rosenberg contributed adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T-cell therapy. Zelig Eshhar and the earliest CAR inventors are not in the credited names, which weakens the allocation.
assessment.maturity: Approved therapies and multi-year remissions confirm efficacy; limits in solid tumors, toxicity and cost remain, but the discovery is mature for hematologic cancers.
uncertainties: Absence of the original CAR concept inventors from the credited set.
Rosenberg's contribution may be better assessed separately as general adoptive immunotherapy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing (nusinersen) gave the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, a clear mechanism-to-medicine story that validated splice-switching oligonucleotides.
assessment.attribution: Krainer elucidated the splicing mechanism and identified the target sequence; Bennett led the antisense chemistry and development at Ionis. A clean two-person configuration, though others in the clinical program and in the SMN gene discovery (Melki, Lefebvre) lie outside this entry.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with robust long-term clinical benefit and independent confirmation; a platform with growing follow-on antisense drugs.
uncertainties: SMN1 gene discovery is a separate foundational contribution not credited here.
Nusinersen's long-term outcomes in treated adults are still being defined.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provides cell-type-specific control of neural activity with light and has reshaped experimental neuroscience, with emerging therapeutic uses in vision restoration.
assessment.attribution: The channelrhodopsin discovery (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and its deployment in neurons (Boyden, Deisseroth, also Miesenböck's earlier genetically targeted photoactivation) are distinct stages; six credited names exceed three places, and any trio will leave out major contributors.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and independently confirmed across thousands of laboratories; recognition is timely though impact on medicine proper is still modest.
uncertainties: Intractable allocation among at least six credible contributors.
Fit with a medicine award rather than a tool-based or physics/chemistry framing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing underlies modern genomics, oncology diagnostics and rare-disease diagnosis, and is among the most broadly enabling technologies in biomedicine.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman (Solexa chemistry) are central, with Mayer (clustered amplification and early parallel sequencing concepts). Other platforms (454, Lynx MPSS, Church and others) are outside the credited set, leaving attribution contestable.
assessment.maturity: Technology has long been validated at global scale; timing is mature and the technology's impact clearly lasting.
uncertainties: Competing contributors to the broader next-generation sequencing field are not credited.
Whether a technology invention fits the prize's discovery emphasis, given the 2020s precedent in methods.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Adult stem-cell-derived organoids from LGR5-positive stem cells enable self-organizing culture of human epithelia, supporting disease modeling, drug testing and personalized medicine.
assessment.attribution: Clevers is the clear conceptual leader (LGR5 stem cells and the organoid system); Sato was the key experimental driver of the original intestinal and human organoid cultures. The pair is coherent, though Sasai and pluripotent-derived organoid pioneers are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Broadly adopted and replicated, but clinical impact is still emerging; moderately mature.
uncertainties: Relative clinical impact is still limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway defines how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity and has implications for infection, autoimmunity, cancer immunotherapy and interferonopathies.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and cGAMP as the second messenger; Barber identified STING. Ishikawa's early STING work and Sun, Wu contributions are also credited, so a two-person prize is defensible but leaves colleagues out.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is well confirmed; therapeutic agonists and antagonists remain in clinical development, so translational validation is incomplete.
uncertainties: Clinical benefit of STING-targeted drugs is not yet established.
Credit division among STING discoverers (Barber, Ishikawa) versus cGAS discoverers (Chen group).
